verses.english: Numbered Discourses 9.6
1. Awakening
Association

verses.pali: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi …pe… āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
verses.english: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:
“Reverends, you should distinguish two two kinds of individual:
those you should associate with, and those you shouldn’t associate with.
You should distinguish two kinds of robes:
those you should wear, and those you shouldn’t wear.
You should distinguish two kinds of almsfood:
that which you should eat, and that which you shouldn’t eat.
You should distinguish two kinds of lodging:
those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.
You should distinguish two kinds of village or town:
those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.
You should distinguish two kinds of country:
those you should frequent, and those you shouldn’t frequent.
You should distinguish two two kinds of individual:
those you should associate with, and those you shouldn’t associate with.’

verses.pali: iti kho panetaṁ vuttaṁ. Kiñcetaṁ paṭicca vuttaṁ?
verses.english: That’s what I said, but why did I say it?
Well, should you know of an individual:

verses.pali: ‘imaṁ kho me puggalaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti;
verses.english: ‘When I associate with this individual, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.

verses.pali: ye ca kho me pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā te ca kasirena samudāgacchanti;
verses.english: And the necessities of life that a renunciate requires—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—are hard to come by.

verses.pali: yassa camhi atthāya agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito so ca me sāmaññattho na bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī’ti, tenāvuso, puggalena so puggalo rattibhāgaṁ vā divasabhāgaṁ vā saṅkhāpi anāpucchā pakkamitabbaṁ nānubandhitabbo.
verses.english: And the goal of the ascetic life for which I went forth from the lay life to homelessness is not being fully developed.’ In this case you should leave that individual at that very time of the day or night, without asking. You shouldn’t follow them.
Whereas, should you know of an individual:

verses.pali: ‘imaṁ kho me puggalaṁ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyanti;
verses.english: ‘When I associate with this individual, unskillful qualities grow, and skillful qualities decline.

verses.pali: ye ca kho me pabbajitena jīvitaparikkhārā samudānetabbā cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā te ca appakasirena samudāgacchanti;
verses.english: But the necessities of life that a renunciate requires—robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicines and supplies for the sick—are easy to come by.

verses.pali: yassa camhi atthāya agārasmā anagāriyaṁ pabbajito so ca me sāmaññattho na bhāvanāpāripūriṁ gacchatī’ti, tenāvuso, puggalena so puggalo saṅkhāpi anāpucchā pakkamitabbaṁ nānubandhitabbo.
verses.english: However, the goal of the ascetic life for which I went forth from the lay life to homelessness is not being fully developed.’ In this case you should leave that individual after reflecting, without asking. You shouldn’t follow them.

verses.english: ‘When I associate with this individual, unskillful qualities decline, and skillful qualities grow.

those you should associate with, and those you shouldn’t associate with.’
